notes: The claimed-module map keeps all same-module blocks but still overrides child imports per ConfigResource rather than per instance, so a parent import of one instance drops the child's other instances; tests are thorough (unit fixture, plan and apply) but never exercise that case.

Keeps every block declared in the same module, which fixes the reported for_each case, but a parent import of one instance still silently drops the child's import blocks for other instances of that resource; dedup belongs at instance level after expansion, as in the reference.

Fixes the same-module for_each case by returning a slice, but a parent import of any one instance now overrides every child import for that resource, so child imports of other instances are silently dropped; deduplication should happen per instance after expansion, as the reference does.
Same coarse semantics as C1 (any ancestor block for the resource drops all child blocks), using a hand-rolled ancestor helper and an O(n^2) scan, with only a single root-module regression test.

Compares static instance keys so parent/child overrides work for distinct static instances, but if either block is dynamic it treats the whole resource as covered; this silently drops same-module for_each or mixed static/dynamic import blocks, ignores module instance keys, and needs an exported configs helper re-parsed in an O(n^2) loop.

Instance-level static dedup handles the reported and cross-module static cases, but treating any dynamic target as covering the whole resource still silently drops a static block alongside a for_each block in the same module, and it exports and renames a configs function to do so.

Per-instance dedup for static targets handles parent overriding distinct child instances and mixed same-module blocks, but two dynamic blocks for one resource in a module still lose the second, a parent static plus child dynamic pair can let the child win, and it duplicates configs' static-parse logic.

Dedups static targets per instance, so the reported case and cross-module distinct instances work, but it duplicates configs.parseImportToStatic, drops a second dynamic (for_each) block for the same resource even within one module, and in mixed static/dynamic parent-child cases the child can overwrite the parent at expansion.

Correct and complete, including the `{}` branch, but repeats inline `wasQuoted == 0` / `Quoted()` checks everywhere with mixed style instead of a helper; tests are thorough, including an end-to-end httpcaddyfile adapter test.

Functionally equivalent to the reference, but uses repetitive inline checks that mix `Quoted()` and `wasQuoted == 0`. Tests are very thorough, including an end-to-end httpcaddyfile adapter test in another package.

Clean Token helper methods applied across the dispenser and parser, essentially matching the reference; however, it leaves the quoted-`"{}"` branch in directive() untouched, so a quoted `"{}"` on a new line at nesting 0 is still wrongly absorbed into the previous segment.

Uses the same clean Token-method approach as C3 but leaves the `p.Val() == "{}"` branch unguarded. A quoted `"{}"` at the start of a line can therefore still bypass the new-segment check, which the reference fixed.

Mirrors the reference almost exactly, including the unquoted `{}` fix, with idiomatic Token helpers and strong tests covering NextArg/NextBlock, existing parse tables, snippets, named routes and import blocks.

Closely mirrors the reference with unexported Token methods applied at every brace site, including the quoted `{}` branch. Tests cover dispenser args and blocks, parse tables, snippets, named routes and import blocks.

Complete fix that includes the unquoted `{}` branch, via a bounds-checked Dispenser.isUnquotedVal helper; doImport uses inline checks instead, which is slightly inconsistent, and the tests are adequate but narrower (two NextBlock cases plus one snippet parse).

Covers every structural brace check that the reference touches, using a bounds-safe `isUnquotedVal` Dispenser helper, and fixes the quoted `{}` branch too. Its tests cover NextBlock and snippet parsing but do not test the exact issue input.
